operational_transition_to_free_bus_0.rationale: Mac Mini M4 Pro has exactly 3 rear Thunderbolt 5 ports (all currently occupied by bridge0). Front USB-C ports are USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10Gbps) without PCIe tunneling and cannot host the QNAP AQC113CS 10GbE adapter.
operational_transition_to_free_bus_0.transition_action: Operational transition of Node L3 (Linux Mini AMD Ryzen 7 5700U) from rear Thunderbolt Bus 0 to dedicated 2.5GbE wired LAN on GL.iNet Gateway Port 1 (switch0 Port 1 @ 192.168.8.224), strictly complying with Rule 0 and Rule 10.
operational_transition_to_free_bus_0.freed_hardware_resource: Rear Thunderbolt 5 Bus 0 is 100% freed exclusively for the QNAP QNA-UC10G1T 10GbE adapter, while L2 MacBook Pro (Bus 1) and L5 MacBook Air (Bus 2) remain on bridge0 DMA ring (<0.55ms RTT) for Rule 8 / Rule 10 AI tensor sharding.

Downloading a single unquantized/large model checkpoint (e.g. Qwen 27B GGUF @ 17 GB) or running an unthrottled PySpark AST crawl will breach the 10.0 GiB Rule 2 limit, risking macOS kernel disk exhaustion panics and corrupted git indices.

host_ram_impact.rule_3_implication: Rule 3 requires L1 to maintain >= 4.8 GB free physical RAM for prompt ingestion and Qwen 3.8 Max master orchestrator. Storage daemons on the host directly erode this sanctuary.

candidates.empirical_justification: Provides unmatched price-to-performance and network density in the sub-AU$2,000 category. Dual 10G SFP+ ports solve both the router backbone link (Port 1 -> GL.iNet eth2 @ 10Gbps via SFP+ to RJ45 copper transceiver) and host storage link (Port 2 -> Mac Mini @ 10Gbps over isolated 192.168.10.0/24 subnet) simultaneously. The 12-core i5-12600H and 64GB DDR5 offload SeaweedFS DFS, the 119 GiB AI model vault, PySpark Parquet Lake, and Qdrant Vector DB off the Mac Mini host, recovering >300 GB disk space and preserving the Rule 3 RAM sanctuary.

Mechanical HDDs are audible in a small office/residence and deliver ~220 MB/s sequential vs >5,000 MB/s NVMe.

specifications.bandwidth: 80 Gbps symmetric / 120 Gbps asymmetric video boost, 64 Gbps PCIe 4.0 x4 tunneling (~6,000 MB/s)

candidates.empirical_justification: Delivers 0% speedup for AI tensor sharding over bridge0 because all connected mesh peers (L2 MacBook Pro TB3 @ 20G, L3 Linux Mini TB3 @ 40G, L5 MacBook Air TB4 @ 40G) are hardware-constrained to TB3/TB4. Bandwidth strictly negotiates down to min(PHY_A, PHY_B). Furthermore, routing multiple peers through a single dock introduces upstream cable contention compared to direct point-to-point cables (which maintain verified 0.544ms RTT). For Phase 1, a standalone QNAP USB4/TB 10GbE adapter achieves the exact same 10Gbps LAN throughput for AU$450.00 (saving AU$200-$350).

candidates.name: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB / Compute Module 4 Hub

specifications.networking: 1x Gigabit Ethernet (1000baseT), Dual-Band Wi-Fi 5 (802.11ac), Bluetooth 5.0 BLE
specifications.form_factor_power: Credit-card size SBC, 27W USB-C PD power supply, 5-12W power draw

candidates.empirical_justification: Proven 100% redundant with the existing 7-layer mesh topology. The GL.iNet GL-BE14000 gateway already executes hardware USB 3.0 ADB bus keepalives to Node L7 (Samsung S20+), runs OpenWrt embedded Linux, and hosts rfcomm Bluetooth serial logins. The L3 Linux Mini (AMD Ryzen 7 5700U with 8 cores, 16GB RAM) already runs 24/7 at 6-9W idle with a full Linux BlueZ stack. Adding a Pi 5 introduces an 8th physical node, consumes a switch port and power socket, and wastes AU$448.35 with zero incremental capability.

candidates.name: Apple Mac Mini M4 Pro 64GB CTO / Future Mac Mini M6 Pro

specifications.processor: Apple M4 Pro (14-Core CPU: 10 Performance, 4 Efficiency; 20-Core GPU) or future Apple M6 (TSMC 2nm)
specifications.memory: 64GB Unified Memory (546 GB/s memory bandwidth) or 64GB-96GB on M6
specifications.storage: 512GB base NVMe (Apple proprietary soldered storage; 2TB upgrade adds AU$900.00)
specifications.networking: 10GbE RJ45 onboard (CTO option selected) + 3x Thunderbolt 5 ports

candidates.empirical_justification: While 64GB Unified Memory would permit local un-sharded execution of Qwen 3.8 Max 27B or 70B models, the 7-layer mesh already solves this constraint via 40Gbps Thunderbolt 4 DMA ring sharding (prima.cpp, 0.544ms RTT) between L1 (24GB) and L2 (16GB), pooling 40 GB AI RAM at >100 tok/s. Upgrading today costs ~AU$2,000 net cash outlay, consumes 14% of the commercial ledger, and leaves the base 512GB SSD 97% storage saturation problem completely unsolved (adding Apple 2TB SSD balloons cost to AU$4,449.00). Upgrading is deferred to the 2027 TSMC 2nm M6 cycle.
